welcome.subtitle: Your mods, stored once. As many setups as you like.

notice.title: How FS Passion works
notice.at_start: Show this window when the application starts

blocks.key: First of all: we recommend making a backup copy of all your mods on another drive. It is essential, as before any operation on important files.

blocks.p: FS Passion lets you create, quickly and easily, as many Farming Simulator setups as you like, while keeping a single copy of your mods in their original folder.
Switch from one setup to another in 1 click!

Your mods folder can be on any drive: FS Passion adapts. There is nothing to create, move or rename by hand. Drive full? Add up to two mods folders on other drives (Settings → Game and paths): their mods join setups like the others.

ul: Create your setups with the magic “＋ Setup” button found on maps: the map and its dependencies become the setup in one click.
Then sort the other mods into the common mods, present in every setup.
Click “Apply”: the game will load the chosen setup the next time it starts.
New mods: download them as usual, then click “Search for new mods” at the top of the list. FS Passion puts them in the mods folder of the right game version.
To delete mods, do it in FS Passion (“Delete permanently” in the action bar) rather than in File Explorer: they are then removed from the lists and setups at the same time, and go to the Recycle Bin.
Renaming a mod (F2 key) detaches it from the ModHub: it will no longer receive updates.

blocks.p: Nothing to do: updates downloaded by the game are recovered when it closes, or the next time FS Passion starts. The old version is set aside in “Old versions”. If the game downloads an older version number than yours (often a mod you modified), FS Passion asks you which one to keep.
FS Passion itself: when a new version is released, a dot appears on the Settings gear and “New version” next to the version number, at the bottom. Settings → Application → “Install the update”.
Settings → Application → “Export” saves your setups, common mods and settings to a file. “Import” brings them back, after a reinstall or on another PC.
“Stop using FS Passion” (Settings → Application) gives the game its original setting back and removes the setup folders. Your mods are never touched.

rights.title: Rights for mods on other drives
rights.intro: For a mod stored on another drive to join a setup, FS Passion creates a symbolic link. Windows only allows it with Developer Mode or administrator rights, and neither is active.
rights.standard: Your Windows account is a standard account: getting administrator rights would run FS Passion under another account, with other folders and settings. Developer Mode is the right choice.
rights.admin_title: Always run FS Passion as administrator
rights.admin_text: FS Passion ticks “Run this program as an administrator” for you (Properties → Compatibility), for your account only, then restarts. Consequences:
rights.uac: Windows asks for confirmation every time FS Passion starts.
rights.game_normal: The game and its platform are still started with normal rights, through Windows Explorer. Launch arguments then go through the platform (Steam, Epic Games), as usual.
rights.no_drop: Windows blocks dragging files from Explorer onto FS Passion. No effect today: FS Passion does not use that gesture.
rights.dev_title: Or: turn on Windows Developer Mode
rights.dev_text: Windows Settings → System → For developers → “Developer Mode”. No other consequence for FS Passion. Then come back here and click “Check again”.
rights.without: Without these rights, the additional folders stay saved: their mods are listed, but do not join any setup.
rights.missing: Windows refuses symbolic links: mods on other drives are listed, but do not join any setup.
rights.ok: Symbolic links allowed (FS Passion runs as administrator): mods on other drives join setups.
rights.ok_dev: Symbolic links allowed (Windows Developer Mode): mods on other drives join setups.
rights.unknown: Rights for symbolic links have not been checked yet.
rights.admin_on: FS Passion is set to always run as administrator.
rights.restarting: FS Passion is restarting as administrator. Confirm the Windows prompt.
rights.now_ok: Symbolic links allowed: apply your setups again so mods on other drives can join them.
rights.flag_failed: The “Run as administrator” setting could not be changed.
rights.ok_plain: Symbolic links allowed: mods on other drives join setups.
rights.admin_once_text: FS Passion restarts as administrator this time only; to be redone at each launch. Developer Mode avoids this. Consequences:

older.title: Older version downloaded by the game

intro.one: The game downloaded a mod whose version number is older than yours. It was set aside, nothing was replaced. What do you want to do?
intro.other: The game downloaded {count} mods whose version number is older than yours. They were set aside, nothing was replaced. What do you want to do?

older.versions: Your version: {mine} · version downloaded by the game: {game}
older.use_tip: The game's version takes the place of yours, in its mods folder; yours is set aside in “Old versions”. All setups follow.
older.help: This is often a mod you modified: the ModHub does not compare version numbers, it offers its original. Either way nothing is deleted: the file you do not keep stays in the “Recovered” or “Old versions” folder, next to your setups.
older.gone: This file is no longer in the “Recovered” folder: nothing was changed.
older.failed: The game's version of {name} could not be put in place ({detail}). Your version did not change.

stop.running: Close {game} first: its setting must be restored while the game is closed.
stop.folders_failed: The setup folders could not be deleted.
stop.closed: FS Passion is closed. The game has its original setting back.
stop.export_first: Before going on, export your configuration: you will get your setups back if you return to FS Passion.
stop.intro: FS Passion will give the game its original setting back, then remove the setup folders (they only contain links):
stop.no_version: No game version is configured: there is nothing to restore.
stop.mods_safe: Your mods folders are never touched, nor “Old versions” and “Recovered”, which contain mods set aside.
stop.admin_flag: The “Run this program as an administrator” setting set by FS Passion will be removed.
stop.understand: I understand: the game will no longer load FS Passion setups.

plan.restore: The game loads its original folder again: {dir}
plan.deactivate: The custom mods folder is turned off: the game goes back to its usual “mods” folder.
plan.missing: gameSettings.xml not found: nothing to restore.

done.title: FS Passion is no longer used
done.text: Done. The game has its original setting back.
done.partial: Done, except for at least one version: see below. The log has the details.

version.other: original setting restored, {count} setup folders removed

set_aside.other: {count} files found in the setup folders were set aside in “Recovered”.

stop.stopped: FS Passion is no longer used: close it.

hint.caption: Fancy a guided tour?
hint.body: Click the light bulb: in one minute, FS Passion shows you the essentials of its interface. It stays there so you can replay the tour whenever you like.

versions.caption: Your game version
versions.body:
Hover over this logo: the Farming Simulator versions appear. Click the one you want to manage.
Versions that are not installed are greyed out. Each version has its own mods and its own setups.
versions.picked: Selected: its mods and setups are shown

parties.caption: Your setups: the heart of FS Passion
parties.body:
One click switches from one setup to another: its map and all its dependencies follow.
Full setup: all your mods, to update them in the game.
Empty setup: no mods, to test the original game.
parties.full_tip: All mods: to run mod updates in the game
parties.empty_tip: No mods: to test the original game

tools.caption: Create, duplicate, rename, delete
tools.body:
Actions on the selected setup.
Tip: on a map in “All mods”, the “＋ Setup” button creates the setup with the map and all its dependencies, in one click.

common.caption: Common mods
common.body:
The vehicles, tools and gameplay scripts you want in all your setups.
They are on by default; if needed, turn them off for a single setup.
common.on: Common mods included in this setup
common.off: Turned off for this setup only

apply.caption: Apply
apply.body:
Applies the selected setup: it is the one the game will load the next time it starts.
The button lights up as long as the selected setup is not applied.
apply.done: Applied: the game will load it next time it starts

buttons.caption: Theme, notifications, settings
buttons.body: Light or dark interface, message history, settings… And the light bulb, to replay this tour whenever you like.

list1.caption: All mods
list1.body:
Your whole mods folder, sorted by category: DLC, maps, other mods…
A mod always stays here, whatever you do in the other lists. “Unsorted” mods are in no list: the game does not see them.
[Ctrl] + [F]: search for a mod or an author.

downloads.caption: Newly downloaded mods
downloads.body:
This button looks for the mods you just downloaded in your Downloads folder.
FS Passion detects the game version of each one and, with your agreement, puts it in the right mods folder.
It also does this at startup: see Settings → Application → Downloads.
downloads.found: Each one goes to the mods folder of its game version

list2.caption: Setup mods
list2.body:
The mods of the selected setup: its map, its dependencies, its own mods.
The game loads them on top of the common mods.

list3.caption: Common mods
list3.body:
The mods present in all your setups: tractors, tools, scripts…
Sort them here once: every setup gets them.

select.caption: Multiple selection
select.body:
[Ctrl] + click: add or remove a mod from the selection.
[Shift] + click: select a whole range.
[Ctrl] + [A]: select everything in the list; [Esc]: clear the selection.
As soon as a mod is selected, an action bar appears at the bottom.

move.caption: Drag and drop
move.body:
To “Setup mods” or “Common mods”: it is a copy, the mod stays in “All mods”.
Between these two lists: it is a move. Hold [Ctrl] while dropping to copy.
To “All mods”, or the [Del] key: the mod is removed from the list. Its file is never deleted.

rows.d: Search for a mod or an author
Add or remove a mod from the selection
Clear the selection, or cancel a drag
Copy instead of moving (between lists 2 and 3)
Remove from list 2 or 3 (the file stays)
Create a setup with the map and its dependencies
Select and move around with the keyboard

close.caption: Close without quitting
close.body:
The cross closes the window, but FS Passion keeps running in the background, in the notification area next to the clock.
To bring it back: the “^” arrow on the taskbar, then the FS icon. To really close it: “Quit”, bottom right, or right-click the icon.
You can change this in Settings → Application → Window.
close.tip_close: Close: FS Passion moves to the notification area
close.tip_icon: Click: FS Passion comes back · Right-click: Quit

end.caption: Over to you!
end.body: Replay this tour whenever you like with the light bulb, or in Settings → Help and about.
